---
name: notorganic-eval-account
description: "The dedicated Not Organic DID for Twyne's paid evals, where its credentials live, the session-version quirk, and how its spend cap works"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: cd19f63d-429e-4f08-9943-b87e47cad0b8
  modified: 2026-10-23T07:34:14.468Z
---

Created 2026-10-23 at the user's request ("make a DID for this eval", cap $50):

- DID `did:plc:h7t2qykaxwf6s7iez6pmhs45`, handle `twyne-evals.pds.notorganic.info`, created on Not Organic's own PDS. It has signed in to the portal (id.notorganic.info) once, which makes it a known account there.
- skate: `twyne-eval-did` (the DID) and `twyne-evals-pds-password`. The account email is the user's Gmail plus-address `+twyne-evals`.
- **Session version 0.** The DID has no `didAccounts` row in Not Organic, so set `TWYNE_EVAL_SESSION_VERSION=0`. Without it, the gateway's `inference:begin` throws `session_revoked`, which the gateway does not map, so Twyne sees an opaque 500 `internal_error`.
- **Funding.** The first Twyne call auto-granted the $2.50 `twyne_welcome` lot; the portal's `/api/wallet` view doesn't show it. Any further credit needs an admin grant (Admin → Accounts → Direct grant, product scope Twyne); the cap the user set is $50 total. The production portal secret isn't reachable from this machine; no local notorganic-provider checkout links the prod Convex.
- **Reservations.** Each call reserves its alias ceiling up front (fast $0.25, balanced $0.50, reasoning $2.00), so parallel room calls need several dollars of headroom even though the actual cost is cents.
- **Signing config.** It comes from Twyne's *prod* Convex env: `npx convex env get --prod NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_PRIVATE_KEY` (also `NOTORGANIC_ISSUER` and `NOTORGANIC_AUDIENCE`). The dev deployment has none.

**Gateway state as of 2026-10-23.** The running Not Organic gateway (Railway project `notorganic-provider`, service `gateway`, deployment 03c44bc7 from 2026-10-21) still holds revoked Keenable and TypeSafe keys. The working replacements are staged in its Railway variables (hash-matched against skate's `keenable-api-key@secrets` and `typesafe_api_key`) but not loaded. As a result `/v1/web/search` returns 502 and `/v1/judgement` returns 503 `judgement_invalid_configuration`. Production Twyne's editorial review gate and hosted claim checks are therefore silently off. Railway reports `canRedeploy: false`, so loading the keys needs a fresh build. The user chose not to deploy it on 2026-10-23.

**Eval workaround until that build ships:** `--system-one direct` (Jev with `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, honoured only by the loopback in-process app via `TWYNE_EVAL_JUDGEMENT_TRANSPORT`) and `--research keenable` (`evals/app/keenable-bridge.ts`, `KEENABLE_API_KEY`).

**Output ceiling.** The gateway's default output ceiling is around 4k tokens, and every text alias (fast/balanced/reasoning) routes to Inkling-Small, which can think past it. Twyne's `NO_OUTPUT_CEILING` is now 16,000 (convex/agents.ts).

Related: [[arize-workspace]], [[model-nicknames-for-delegation]].

**Live voice, 2026-10-28.** The gateway's `OPENAI_LIVE_API_KEY` returns 401 `invalid_api_key` from OpenAI. As a result, every Twyne Live session closes in under 1s, and the browser shows "Disconnected before final usage arrived". skate `openai-api-token@secrets` and `openai_api_key@secrets` both pass the `wss://api.openai.com/v1/live/sessions` handshake; `openai-api@secrets` is also dead. The Bun relay (`apps/gateway/src/bun-realtime.ts`) logs nothing when the upstream fails. Fixed the same day: the key was set from `openai_api_key@secrets` and gateway deployment 2cf92906 succeeded. That deploy also loaded the Keenable/TypeSafe keys staged since 10-23, so the gateway-state note above may now be stale.

content.content:
# Autonomous editorial work — change summary

Responds to the Twyne UX improvement brief of 2026-10-19 and to
the product direction that followed it: **Twyne acts without being asked.**
Reviews, research and editors' readings run on their own; buttons remain as
shortcuts and overrides, not as the way work starts.

Released in 0.25.0.

## Principle

A feature that waits for a click before doing its core job is a defect. Each
automatic path has a trigger (folio open, draft change, idle pause, a fresh
quick grade) and spend guards (rate floors, session caps, dedupe by draft
fingerprint). Empty states say what Twyne is about to do, not what to press.
Hosted writers without their own model get the automatic path too.

## 1. Review and research arrive on their own

### Background room — `src/utils/background-room.ts`

| Before                                                                                          | After                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Existing prose counted as read on every open, so an unread draft was never read until Get notes | What the room last read is stored per folio (`background-room-read:<folioId>`). A folio with no record and no notes starts empty and is read on its own; one with notes from before the record existed counts as read |
| Triggered by 500 **net** new words and a 2-minute pause                                         | Triggered by 200 words in new or rewritten paragraphs (`diffParagraphs(...).added`) and a 1-minute pause                                                                                                              |
| `startBackgroundRoom` had no current draft                                                      | `currentText` arms the watcher straight away when the draft holds unread work                                                                                                                                         |

Guards unchanged: `MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (5 min), `MAX_PASSES_PER_SESSION` (8),
`MIN_EDITOR_WORDS` (500) before any reading. `src/routes/editor/index.tsx`
loads the stored baseline and existing notes when the folio opens.

### Rubric — `src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx`

- `autoReadRoom` starts the editors' reading when a live-review quick grade
  arrives for a draft fingerprint the editors have not read, at most every
  `ROOM_READ_FLOOR_MS` (10 min, stored per folio), and only when a hosted
  client or BYOK provider exists.
- `runAnalysis(frontierOnly, quiet)` — a quiet run uses `isReviewing`, so the
  current grade stays on screen instead of the full-panel loader.
- The editors' notes survive later quick checks (`judges` carried forward);
  `judgesFingerprint` marks notes about an earlier version. A reading whose
  draft changed mid-run keeps its notes rather than discarding them.
- Automatic readings snapshot as `automatic` (5-minute spacing) so they cannot
  crowd manual checkpoints out of the 50-entry history; requested readings
  still force a `rubric` checkpoint.
- The Editors tab says `soon` / `reading…` instead of `0`.

### Research — `src/utils/background-research.ts`, `src/utils/research-candidates.ts` (new)

- Hosted writers without their own model: `claimCandidates` finds figures,
  attributed quotations, appeals to authority and dated events by rule;
  one batched Jev request (`candidateRequest`) confirms which need a source
  (Noul ≥ 0.6), with fiction instructed to ignore invented events.
- `ResearchIdleReason` (`waiting`, `too-short`, `no-provider`, `no-claims`,
  `covered`, `pass-done`) replaces the bare "Watching draft".
- Failed passes and failed claims retry on their own at 30 s, 2 min and
  10 min (`scheduleRetry`), then stop and leave the retry control.
- Each Deep trace row says what found / no match / failed means and offers
  Go to the claim.

## 2. Passage grounding and card meaning

- **Quotations** — `src/utils/quote-grounding.ts` (new). `extractQuotations`
  reads paired quotation marks and Markdown block quotes; `resolveQuotation`
  normalises typography, case and whitespace, follows `…` elisions within one
  paragraph, never crosses paragraphs, and breaks ties with the note's
  surrounding words (same paragraph only, stopwords removed). Ties stay
  `ambiguous`; missing text stays `unmatched`. `renderGroundedMarkdown` wraps
  resolved quotations as links after safe Markdown rendering. Links are
  re-resolved on `twyne:content` and again in the editor on click
  (`twyne:reveal-quote`, `findQuotationRange`). Used by the Cast panel notes
  and replies and the in-manuscript note card.
- **Relationship cards** — `flow-conductor.ts` asks a Choice alongside the echo
  Noul (`ECHO_RELATIONS`); shared vocabulary only suppresses the card. The card
  shows both passages and offers That's the connection / Not how I read it.
- **Settled notes** — `src/utils/note-decisions.ts` (new). Intentional / later
  per note, stored on this device (`note-decisions:<folioId>`). A decision
  stands while its anchor still resolves in the draft; `withoutSettled` drops
  repeat notes from the same editor in explicit and background passes, and
  `decisionsDigest` goes to the editors as context.

## 3. Versions — `src/utils/revision-history.ts`, `version-history-panel.tsx`

- `describeRevision` writes one sentence per comparison from the changes
  (rewrote / cut / added, and whose notes the rewrites reached).
- Changes are labelled Rewritten / Cut / New passage with Before and After.
- `notesTouchedBy` shows editor notes whose anchor was in the old passage and
  is gone from the new one — evidence the change reached the note, not proof
  it answered it.
- Optional intent on Save checkpoint (`RevisionSnapshot.intent`) names the
  checkpoint. Counts move under Size of the change.

## Answers to the brief's open questions

- **Cast cards / "further on as you read".** Cast cards are `PersonasPanel`
  notes (`personas-panel.tsx`); the "Further on in this piece" card is an
  `echo` flow item from `flow-conductor.ts`, rendered by `flow-surface.tsx`.
- **Editor review and the manual click.** The quick check never runs the
  editors; the click started their reading. It now starts on its own.
- **"Watching graph".** Research went idle silently when there was no
  provider, the draft was short, no claims were found or all were covered.
  Each is now a named state, and hosted writers have a provider path.
- **Jev's decisions.** Jev confirms echo relevance and relationship, hosted
  research claims, note quality gates, and the quick grade; the relationship
  label and the research claim rows surface those decisions.
- **Revision information.** Snapshots hold full HTML and Typst source, so
  passage-level before/after is exact; intent is now recorded when given, and
  note evidence is derived from stored editor notes.

## Not covered

- Unread markers for finished reviews.
- Rejected relationship readings are dismissed, not recorded as a rejected
  reading.
- Note decisions do not sync between devices.
- Manual screenshots for the Cast notes, echo card, Apparatus Deep trace and
  Version history predate these changes.

## Tests

`quote-grounding.test.ts`, `note-decisions.test.ts`,
`research-candidates.test.ts`, additions to `background-room.test.ts` and
`revision-history.test.ts`; `personas-markdown-wiring.test.ts` updated for the
grounded renderer.

content.content:
# Autonomous editorial work — change summary

Responds to the Twyne UX improvement brief of 2026-10-19 and to
the product direction that followed it: **Twyne acts without being asked.**
Reviews, research and editors' readings run on their own; buttons remain as
shortcuts and overrides, not as the way work starts.

Released in 0.25.0.

## Principle

A feature that waits for a click before doing its core job is a defect. Each
automatic path has a trigger (folio open, draft change, idle pause, a fresh
quick grade) and spend guards (rate floors, session caps, dedupe by draft
fingerprint). Empty states say what Twyne is about to do, not what to press.
Hosted writers without their own model get the automatic path too.

## 1. Review and research arrive on their own

### Background room — `src/utils/background-room.ts`

| Before                                                                                          | After                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Existing prose counted as read on every open, so an unread draft was never read until Get notes | What the room last read is stored per folio (`background-room-read:<folioId>`). A folio with no record and no notes starts empty and is read on its own; one with notes from before the record existed counts as read |
| Triggered by 500 **net** new words and a 2-minute pause                                         | Triggered by 200 words in new or rewritten paragraphs (`diffParagraphs(...).added`) and a 1-minute pause                                                                                                              |
| `startBackgroundRoom` had no current draft                                                      | `currentText` arms the watcher straight away when the draft holds unread work                                                                                                                                         |

Guards unchanged: `MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (5 min), `MAX_PASSES_PER_SESSION` (8),
`MIN_EDITOR_WORDS` (500) before any reading. `src/routes/editor/index.tsx`
loads the stored baseline and existing notes when the folio opens.

### Rubric — `src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx`

- `autoReadRoom` starts the editors' reading when a live-review quick grade
  arrives for a draft fingerprint the editors have not read, at most every
  `ROOM_READ_FLOOR_MS` (10 min, stored per folio), and only when a hosted
  client or BYOK provider exists.
- `runAnalysis(frontierOnly, quiet)` — a quiet run uses `isReviewing`, so the
  current grade stays on screen instead of the full-panel loader.
- The editors' notes survive later quick checks (`judges` carried forward);
  `judgesFingerprint` marks notes about an earlier version. A reading whose
  draft changed mid-run keeps its notes rather than discarding them.
- Automatic readings snapshot as `automatic` (5-minute spacing) so they cannot
  crowd manual checkpoints out of the 50-entry history; requested readings
  still force a `rubric` checkpoint.
- The Editors tab says `soon` / `reading…` instead of `0`.

### Research — `src/utils/background-research.ts`, `src/utils/research-candidates.ts` (new)

- Hosted writers without their own model: `claimCandidates` finds figures,
  attributed quotations, appeals to authority and dated events by rule;
  one batched Jev request (`candidateRequest`) confirms which need a source
  (Noul ≥ 0.6), with fiction instructed to ignore invented events.
- `ResearchIdleReason` (`waiting`, `too-short`, `no-provider`, `no-claims`,
  `covered`, `pass-done`) replaces the bare "Watching draft".
- Failed passes and failed claims retry on their own at 30 s, 2 min and
  10 min (`scheduleRetry`), then stop and leave the retry control.
- Each Deep trace row says what found / no match / failed means and offers
  Go to the claim.

## 2. Passage grounding and card meaning

- **Quotations** — `src/utils/quote-grounding.ts` (new). `extractQuotations`
  reads paired quotation marks and Markdown block quotes; `resolveQuotation`
  normalises typography, case and whitespace, follows `…` elisions within one
  paragraph, never crosses paragraphs, and breaks ties with the note's
  surrounding words (same paragraph only, stopwords removed). Ties stay
  `ambiguous`; missing text stays `unmatched`. `renderGroundedMarkdown` wraps
  resolved quotations as links after safe Markdown rendering. Links are
  re-resolved on `twyne:content` and again in the editor on click
  (`twyne:reveal-quote`, `findQuotationRange`). Used by the Cast panel notes
  and replies and the in-manuscript note card.
- **Relationship cards** — `flow-conductor.ts` asks a Choice alongside the echo
  Noul (`ECHO_RELATIONS`); shared vocabulary only suppresses the card. The card
  shows both passages and offers That's the connection / Not how I read it.
- **Settled notes** — `src/utils/note-decisions.ts` (new). Intentional / later
  per note, stored on this device (`note-decisions:<folioId>`). A decision
  stands while its anchor still resolves in the draft; `withoutSettled` drops
  repeat notes from the same editor in explicit and background passes, and
  `decisionsDigest` goes to the editors as context.

## 3. Versions — `src/utils/revision-history.ts`, `version-history-panel.tsx`

- `describeRevision` writes one sentence per comparison from the changes
  (rewrote / cut / added, and whose notes the rewrites reached).
- Changes are labelled Rewritten / Cut / New passage with Before and After.
- `notesTouchedBy` shows editor notes whose anchor was in the old passage and
  is gone from the new one — evidence the change reached the note, not proof
  it answered it.
- Optional intent on Save checkpoint (`RevisionSnapshot.intent`) names the
  checkpoint. Counts move under Size of the change.

## Answers to the brief's open questions

- **Cast cards / "further on as you read".** Cast cards are `PersonasPanel`
  notes (`personas-panel.tsx`); the "Further on in this piece" card is an
  `echo` flow item from `flow-conductor.ts`, rendered by `flow-surface.tsx`.
- **Editor review and the manual click.** The quick check never runs the
  editors; the click started their reading. It now starts on its own.
- **"Watching graph".** Research went idle silently when there was no
  provider, the draft was short, no claims were found or all were covered.
  Each is now a named state, and hosted writers have a provider path.
- **Jev's decisions.** Jev confirms echo relevance and relationship, hosted
  research claims, note quality gates, and the quick grade; the relationship
  label and the research claim rows surface those decisions.
- **Revision information.** Snapshots hold full HTML and Typst source, so
  passage-level before/after is exact; intent is now recorded when given, and
  note evidence is derived from stored editor notes.

## Not covered

- Unread markers for finished reviews.
- Rejected relationship readings are dismissed, not recorded as a rejected
  reading.
- Note decisions do not sync between devices.
- Manual screenshots for the Cast notes, echo card, Apparatus Deep trace and
  Version history predate these changes.

## Tests

`quote-grounding.test.ts`, `note-decisions.test.ts`,
`research-candidates.test.ts`, additions to `background-room.test.ts` and
`revision-history.test.ts`; `personas-markdown-wiring.test.ts` updated for the
grounded renderer.

content.text:
I found two separate problems. First, the default search route has no backend on prod, so the loop is actually blocked. Second, even with search working, the loop is a single search per sentence with nothing that reads or checks what comes back. I worked this out from the code and the Convex env vars; I didn't run the app.

## 1. Why it looks blocked

Everyone starts on `researchProvider: "hosted"` (`src/types/index.ts:1149`), which sends every search to `api.research.searchSources`.

- **Prod is missing the setting.** It has `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true` but no `RESEARCH_PROVIDER` and no `RESEARCH_API_KEY`. With nothing set, `providerId()` falls back to TinyFish with an empty key (`convex/research.ts:215`), so `liveSearchConfigured()` is false and you get the local stub.
- **The stub becomes a failure on every claim.** `src/utils/background-research.ts:815` turns it into "Live research is not configured. Choose a research provider in Settings…". So the loop finds claims, and then each one fails.
- **Your own AI model doesn't help.** Your model picks the claims, but the search still goes through the hosted route unless you switched to model web search, a search API or MCP in Settings.
- **Local dev always gets stubs.** The dev deployment has no research or Not Organic variables at all.

The fix was already written and never turned on. The comment at `convex/research.ts:368` describes this exact failure: "an Apparatus that never finds a source". The fix is `RESEARCH_PROVIDER=notorganic`, which searches through the writer's linked Not Organic account. It depends on the gateway's `/v1/web/search`, which was returning 502 on Oct 23 because of a stale Keenable key. The Oct 28 gateway deploy should have loaded the new key, but I haven't checked that it did.

## 2. Why it wouldn't match your vision even when it works

Here is what one pass does today:

- **Claim finding (hosted users):** four regexes look for figures, attributed quotes, "studies show" and "in 19xx". Jev then says yes or no to each match (`src/utils/research-candidates.ts`). A named person, a book, a place or a period detail in a novel never matches.
- **The search query is the sentence itself**, cut to 180 characters. Search engines handle that poorly.
- **One search per claim.** A miss is marked done and never retried with a different query in that session (`background-research.ts:554`).
- **It never reads a source.** `fetchSource` exists in Convex, but nothing in `src/` calls it.
- **"Found" only means the search returned something.** Ranking scores snippet length, author, publisher and position (`src/utils/research-targets.ts:373`). Nothing checks that the page supports the claim. The Clairic value-support check exists, but only in the evals.
- **Hard caps:** 5 claims per pass and 25 background sources per folio. After that it stops.
- **It only reacts to sentences already in the draft.** It never researches the Dossier's subject on its own.

If you meant the native GPUI build: its Apparatus has no research transport at all. The parity fixtures mark those captures "blocked" for that reason.

## What I'd do

1. **Unblock it.** Check that gateway search answers, then set `RESEARCH_PROVIDER=notorganic` on prod. Also change `providerId()` to use Not Organic whenever it's enabled and no key is set, so this can't quietly break again. Each search charges the writer's wallet, up to the $0.05 ceiling.
2. **Make it an actual research loop.** For each claim:
   - The model writes a few queries, searches, and fetches the top pages.
   - Clairic or Jev judges each page: supports, contradicts or unrelated.
   - If nothing supports the claim, it rewrites the queries and tries again, within a budget.
   - It saves only sources that support the claim, along with the passage that does. A contradicting source becomes a fact-check note.
   - Hosted claim finding moves from the regexes to Clairic extraction, which already runs through Not Organic.

Do you want me to start with step 1? It changes a prod env var and spends writers' credit, so I need your go-ahead first. Step 2 is the larger build, and I can go straight into it after.

I'm deciding that for providers with a native search tool, I'll auto-route signed-out users to it, since plain model search risks fabricated sources. Providers without one keep the old model-search path only when a user explicitly picks it, and I won't route anyone there automatically. I also need to decide how to label that explicit path, so it's clear it isn't live search.

content.text:
Yes, signed-in writers are fixed now. Signed-out writers are fixed in code that hasn't been released yet.

**Signed in (live now).** `RESEARCH_PROVIDER=notorganic` is set on prod. I ran a search through prod's own code as the eval account and got three real sources back, so signed-in writers on the default setting now find sources. No deploy was needed. Each search is billed to the writer's Not Organic credit, capped at $0.05.

**Signed out (written and tested, not committed or deployed).** The default setting, now called "Automatic" in Settings, picks a route on every search:
- **Signed in:** searches through their Twyne account.
- **Signed out, with a search key:** uses that key. Keenable is now one of the key options.
- **Signed out, AI key only:** uses that model's web search, if it's OpenAI, Anthropic or Google.
- **Signed out, AI key that can't search:** stops with "Nothing to search with" and says what to add.
- **Signed out, no AI key:** shows "Sign in to research". Before, this showed an error.
- Signing in or out re-runs research straight away.

**The indicator.** The Apparatus status line and the Signal card in the board now say who is searching, for example "Searching through your Twyne account" or "Searching with your Keenable key".

**Model web search actually searches now.** It used to ask the model for URLs with no search tool, so it reported pages it remembered. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google models now get their real search tool, and Twyne keeps only pages the search returned. If someone explicitly picks a provider without built-in search, the old behaviour stays, labelled "without live search".

**Can't break again.** If `RESEARCH_PROVIDER` is ever unset, Convex now falls back to Not Organic whenever Not Organic is enabled. That part only takes effect on the next `convex deploy`.

**Checks:**
- The research tests pass, including new ones for the route rules, the source filter, Keenable, and the Not Organic fallback. Typecheck is clean.
- A live OpenAI web search returned 26 results, and all 3 pages it offered were real and kept.
- I couldn't run Anthropic or Google live: the Anthropic key has no credit and the Gemini key is over its quota. Their output shapes are covered by unit tests only.
- I didn't test it in the browser.
- Two existing tests fail on `personas-panel.tsx`, which I didn't change; they expect a `runClientRoomSynthesis` call that isn't in that file.

**Still open:**
- The dev deployment still returns stub results. Setting `RESEARCH_PROVIDER=keenable` and `RESEARCH_API_KEY` there would fix local dev.
- The bigger gap from before is untouched: one search per claim using the raw sentence, and nothing reads the pages or checks that they support the claim.

content.text:
The gap is closed. A source now goes on file only if a passage from it says what the claim says. The changes aren't committed, and the new code isn't on prod yet.

**How each claim is researched now** (`resolveClaim` in `src/utils/background-research.ts`, helpers in `src/utils/research-verify.ts`):
1. **Several queries per claim, up to three.** Hosted claims search on the key terms first ("1903 Wright brothers flew first powered aircraft Kitty Hawk"), not the raw sentence. A model's own query stays first, and quotations are also searched as the exact phrase.
2. **Reads the top three hits** from each search:
   - Signed-in writers: through Not Organic's page fetch. I checked it live: it read the Wright Flyer page from Wikipedia, about 30,000 characters.
   - Writers with their own Keenable key: through Keenable directly.
   - Other search keys can't fetch pages, so those claims are judged on the search snippet.
3. **Takes the passage that matters.** That's the paragraphs that share the claim's names and figures.
4. **Judges each source:** supports, contradicts or unrelated. Being on the same topic doesn't count as support. Jev judges for signed-in writers and your own model otherwise.
5. **If nothing supports the claim, it tries the next query.** A contradicting source is saved and flagged. Search hits that support nothing are no longer saved.
6. **Rate limits pause it instead of failing it.** It waits the "Try again in Ns" the server gives, then continues.

**In the UI:**
- Each claim shows what it's doing live: "search 2 of 3", "reading nps.gov", "checking 3 sources".
- Settled claims read "2 supports", "contradicted" (in red) or "unsourced".
- Saved sources are stamped "supports" or "contradicts" and quote the passage, in place of the old "why:" line.
- The Deep Trace text says what was done, for example "Searched 3 ways and read 6 pages; nothing said what this claim says".

**Local dev:** the dev deployment now uses Keenable with the key from skate. I pushed the Convex code there and a dev search returned real results.

**Checks:**
- New end-to-end tests for the loop pass. They cover trying a second query after a miss, keeping a contradiction flagged, and never filing unrelated hits.
- I also added unit tests for the queries, passage picking, verdicts and the Not Organic page fetch. Both typechecks pass.
- I haven't run it in the browser.
- The two failing `personas-panel.tsx` tests are unchanged.

**Costs:**
- **Spend:** on the account route each claim can now cost up to 3 searches plus 9 page reads on the writer's Not Organic credit, where it used to be one search. In practice it stops at the first supporting source.
- **Speed:** free-tier writers are limited to 5 searches a minute, so a full pass can now take a few minutes. It waits; it doesn't fail.

**Still to do:** the new client code and Convex code need a release and a `convex deploy` to reach writers. Prod search already works through the env var. Should I commit this on the branch and open a PR?

# Deploying Twyne

Twyne ships as a Qwik City SSR app. The browser bundle is built by Vite into
`dist/`, the SSR server entry into `server/`, and `server.js` (Node `http`)
serves both and listens on `$PORT`.

## Railway (primary)

The repo is configured for [Railway](https://railway.com) via `railway.json`
(`builder: RAILPACK`) and [`railpack.json`](https://railpack.com) — Railpack is
Railway's successor to Nixpacks:

- **Install** (Bun): `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- **Build** (Bun): `bash scripts/railway-build.sh` — runs Convex deploy + Vite
  client + Vite SSR server. If `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` is unset, the script
  degrades to a frontend-only build (backend left untouched).
- **Start** (Node): `node server.js`
- **Healthcheck**: `GET /`

> The `build` step is auto-generated by Railpack from the Node provider
> (uses the mise step to install `bun` + `node`, then runs
> `bun install --frozen-lockfile`). We only override the `build` step to
> inject the Convex deploy + Vite build via `scripts/railway-build.sh` —
> the script is required because the inline `if/then/else` with nested
> single-quoted `&&` strings gets mangled by the build step's shell
> serialization.

`railpack.json` pins `node: 20` + `bun: 1` so the runtime image has `node`
available for the start command (`server.js` uses `node:http`), while Bun does
the install and Vite build.

### One-time setup

1. **Create / link the service** (already linked to `Diogenesoftoronto/twyne`):

   ```bash
   railway add --service twyne --repo Diogenesoftoronto/twyne
   ```

   Railway auto-deploys on every push to the connected branch.

2. **Set environment variables** (see `.env.example` for the full list). The
   `VITE_*` values are baked in at build time, so they must be set on the
   service before the first build:

   ```bash
   railway variables \
     --set "CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=prod:your-deployment|..." \
     --set "VITE_CONVEX_URL=https://your-deployment.convex.cloud" \
     --set "VITE_CONVEX_SITE_URL=https://your-deployment.convex.site" \
     --set "BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=..." \
     --set "BETTER_AUTH_URL=https://www.twyne.love" \
     --set "SITE_URL=https://www.twyne.love"
   ```

   `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` is the production **deploy key** from the Convex
   dashboard (Settings → Deploy keys). The build step uses it to push the
   backend; without it the build only ships the frontend. `PORT` is injected by
   Railway automatically — do not set it.

3. **Custom domain**: in the Railway service → Settings → Networking, add
   `www.twyne.love` and point the DNS `CNAME` at the generated Railway target.
   Until the domain resolves, auth callbacks that expect `https://www.twyne.love`
   will not complete — use the `*.up.railway.app` URL or temporarily set
   `BETTER_AUTH_URL`/`SITE_URL` to it while testing.

### Convex in production

`VITE_CONVEX_URL` should point at a **production** Convex deployment, not a dev
one. The Railway build now runs `npx convex deploy` (gated on `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY`)
as part of the build step, so the backend deploys on every push alongside the
frontend — no separate manual deploy needed.

Sign-in is through Not Organic. ATProto is a separate publishing connection;
Twyne’s email-code and passkey routes are retired. Register each public sign-in
origin with Not Organic, including its `/auth/notorganic/` callback.

Server-side Convex secrets (`NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_PRIVATE_KEY`,
`NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_KEY_ID`, `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED`,
`NOTORGANIC_TWYNE_PRO_V2_ENABLED`, `POSTHOG_PROJECT_API_KEY`,

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Railway build step: deploy Convex backend (when key is configured), then
# build the Qwik City frontend + SSR server.
#
# Gating: when CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY is unset (frontend-only deploys, preview
# environments, local re-runs) we still build the frontend but skip the
# backend push.

set -euo pipefail

if [ -n "${CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo "==> Deploying Convex backend"
  # 1.46 fixes index-removal review with deploy-only keys. Keep CI deployment
  # tooling explicit even when the app's lockfile pins an older client.
  npx --yes convex@1.46.0 deploy --cmd 'bun run build.client && bun run build.server'
else
  echo "==> CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY not set — building frontend only, skipping convex deploy"
  bun run build.client
  bun run build.server
fi

Tool names may include a harness-normalized MCP prefix, such as `mcp__t3_code__delegate_task`; the semantics are the same. Some harnesses attach optional MCP servers lazily: if an initial tool-catalog scan does not show T3 tools, do not conclude that cross-provider delegation is unavailable. Make one bounded direct attempt using the known T3 tool name on the next tool step. In Codex code mode, for example, call `tools.mcp__t3_code__orchestrator_capabilities({})` before reporting that the capability is absent. Keep polling/wait loops bounded, do not duplicate active work, and use stable `clientRequestId` values when retrying tools that accept them.

ACP fallback: some ACP agents accept the injected MCP server but fail to expose its tools. When the T3 tools are absent and `T3_ACP_MCP_NODE` is present, call the same tools through the terminal: `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$T3_ACP_MCP_NODE" ${T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT:+"$T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT"} acp-mcp-call orchestrator_capabilities '{}'` (`T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT` is unset when T3 runs as a standalone executable). Delegate with `acp-mcp-call delegate_task '{"task":"...","target":{"providerInstanceId":"...","model":"..."},"mode":"async","clientRequestId":"..."}'`. This is the supported T3 transport fallback, not an ordinary shell-based substitute for delegation.

### Showing visuals

When a chart, table, diagram, image collage, or mockup would say more than prose, build a self-contained HTML page, check it with `html_preview`, then publish it with `html_render` before your final reply. The reader sees the page above that reply, so don't announce or restate it; add only what it doesn't say.

- When model options are requested or the child keeps the parent's provider instance and model with nonempty `inheritedOptions` from `orchestrator_capabilities`, use `delegate_task` even for native-supported models. Native subagents cannot reliably apply T3 model options. Read the selected model's descriptors from `orchestrator_capabilities` and put settings in `target.options`, not only in the prompt. Claude commonly uses {"effort":"max","fastMode":true}; Codex uses {"reasoningEffort":"max","serviceTier":"priority"}. Do not translate max to high or ignore unsupported settings: report a capability mismatch. Options inherit only for the same provider instance and model; explicit entries override individual values, and [] or {} clears them. Check the returned providerInstanceId, model, and options against the requested selection.


### Background work you wait on

Before you end your turn to wait for a background command or Monitor you started, such as tests, a build, or a CI wait, call `t3_background_wait` with its task ID. The thread then stays in the user's Working list until that task ends, instead of returning to them early. Do not mark a dev server, a watcher, or anything else you leave running.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_background_wait
tools.description: Keep this thread in the user's Working list and out of their inbox while you wait for background work. Start a background command or Monitor first. Call this before you end your turn if you will act on its result when it wakes you. In taskIds, give the ID shown when the task started. The thread stays in Working until the task ends. The user is not told the work is done. Do not mark work you leave running, such as a dev server or watcher. Unmarked commands and monitors never keep the thread in Working. Pass waiting=false to remove the mark. This does not stop the task. IDs that are not running return in unmatched and change nothing. Only Claude threads support this tool. Other providers return an error.

content.text:
I pushed the research loop to `main` as `ea1e7ddc`, rebased onto v0.27.0, and Railway is building it now. Before pushing, the client and server builds passed in a clean worktree, along with the type build, 49 research tests and 42 Convex tests. This deploy runs `convex deploy` as well, so the backend changes go out with it.
